sections.label: What is new
sections.text: The study applies low-input iCUT&Tag to 12 fruit species from nine families, with input as low as approximately 500 nuclei. sections.text: This is a direct reference for asking whether contrasting ripening systems share chromatin-level regulation. The pepper atlas already includes H3K27ac, but H3K9ac and H3K27ac are not interchangeable. The study suggests an additional regulatory layer worth testing beyond the four histone marks currently profiled.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: A recurring association across species does not establish a shared causal mechanism in all species. The original digest was based on searchable information and a user-supplied abstract; figures and supplementary materials were not fully checked.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: Examine nucleus isolation and measures against metabolite interference, stage and ortholog matching, and how SlHDA1 perturbation supports a mechanistic connection between acetylation and ripening.

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: The authors develop SunTag-NOVA by combining the chromatin-associated factor TRBIP1, a methylation-editing module and CHLAMY. The reported advance concerns both targeted methylation efficiency and mitigation of widespread off-target methylation and developmental defects associated with direct-fusion designs.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: The approach links locus-specific methylation editing to chromatin-associated factors while considering efficiency and specificity together. Target-site effects, genome-wide off-target profiles and developmental phenotypes should all inform the assessment.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: For candidate DMRs from the 22-tissue atlas, this suggests a way to ask whether methylation at a particular locus is sufficient to change expression without changing the underlying DNA sequence, rather than relying only on WGBS–RNA correlations.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: Research proposal: prioritize clearly defined DMRs with interpretable expression changes for future causal tests. Measure local methylation, nearby gene expression and off-target effects together. This is a proposed experiment, not a result already demonstrated in pepper.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: Focus on target selection, genome-wide off-target assessment and inheritance of editing effects. Consider how to build controlled causal experiments around the atlas’s key DMRs.

papers.title: Removal of seed coat H3K27me3 in Arabidopsis requires noncanonical functions of brassinosteroid receptors

en.heading: Active H3K27me3 removal and the initiation of tissue development

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: The study reports that seed-coat development requires not only cessation of further PRC2-mediated H3K27me3 deposition, but also active removal of existing H3K27me3 by JMJ proteins including REF6 and ELF6. Loss of BRI1 is associated with elevated H3K27me3, while BRI1 and BRL3 participate through noncanonical and canonical brassinosteroid pathways, respectively.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: In seed-coat cells undergoing limited division, H3K27me3 cannot simply be diluted through replication and must instead be removed enzymatically. This provides an explanation for how some Polycomb targets can be activated during a developmental transition.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: This resembles pepper K5 genes that lose H3K27me3 and increase expression during ripening. It motivates examination of pepper REF6/ELF6/JMJ13 homologs, BRI1/BRL3 and BZR/BES1, including their expression, footprints and candidate target regions, rather than considering PRC2 subunits alone.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: Research proposal: identify genes that lose H3K27me3 and gain ATAC/H3K27ac signals during tissue transitions without obvious proliferation. Such patterns may be consistent with active demethylation rather than passive dilution, but the distinction still requires evidence.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: The original digest described strong local H3K27me3 and genetic evidence but noted the lack of a complete tissue-specific H3K27me3 genome-wide atlas. The study therefore does not directly define all genomic JMJ targets.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: Prioritize JMJ mutant phenotypes, genetic separation of BRI1 and BRL3 functions, and the model explaining why stopping PRC2 deposition alone is insufficient to eliminate pre-existing H3K27me3.

papers.title: Unpacking Chromatin Accessibility with Fiber-seq

en.heading: Fiber-seq for single-molecule chromatin accessibility

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: This work discusses experimental design and analysis pitfalls for plant Fiber-seq. The technique can resolve accessible regions, nucleosome positioning and internal TF footprints along individual long DNA molecules, rather than producing only population-average accessibility peaks.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: Key practices include controlling single-molecule adenine methylation, sequencing depth and overall labeling rates across samples. Long-read mapping bias, per-fiber state inference and differential-accessibility analysis also require attention.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: Fiber-seq could provide orthogonal validation of pepper ATAC-seq and TF-footprinting, particularly when distinguishing mixed cell states within a fruit stage from genuinely changing accessible regions. It is also methodologically relevant to the repeat-rich Capsicum genome.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: Research proposal: select regions with intermediate accessibility or bulk signals that are difficult to interpret and evaluate whether single-molecule validation is worthwhile. Tissue comparisons must consider cell composition and labeling efficiency rather than attributing all signal differences to accessibility changes.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: This is a methods-oriented preprint. Labeling rates, coverage and mapping bias can influence interpretation, and Fiber-seq and ATAC-seq signals should not be treated as equivalent measurements.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: Read the quality-control and differential-accessibility sections first, especially labeling controls, single-molecule state definitions and comparisons with population-average measurements.

papers.title: Positional grammar of transcription factor binding partitions developmental and stress-response regulation in plants

en.heading: TF binding-position grammar in development and stress responses

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: The study combines conserved binding sites for 244 TFs with single-nucleus accessibility, cell-type expression and hormone-response data to investigate the positional grammar of plant TF binding sites.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: Accessibility close to the TSS alone is a poor predictor of cell-type-specific expression. Binding sites in distal promoters, introns and rare-cell-specific accessible regions are more informative for development, whereas broadly accessible proximal sites are associated more strongly with rapid stress and hormonal responses.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: This motivates stratifying proximal, distal, intronic and CDS-associated footprints in the pepper ripening network instead of assigning every accessible peak to its nearest gene.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: Research proposal: annotate atlas ACRs by position and tissue specificity, and incorporate these properties into enhancer-candidate prioritization. First compare motif and footprint distributions across these classes before revising TF–target assignment.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: A relationship between binding-site position and function does not establish that a particular ACR regulates a particular gene. Nearest-gene assignment and TSS accessibility alone are not causal evidence; application to pepper needs validation.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: Focus on positional stratification, cell-type specificity and the developmental versus stress-response framework, then revisit distal and intronic ACR annotations.

sections.label: What to read first

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: First understand the SWI3B–MTA interaction and the proposed connections to transcript stability, WOX8 and auxin polarity; a figure-by-figure reading is not yet essential.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research

sections.label: What to read first

en.heading: CrJAG connects chromatin state to fruit shape

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: CrJAG interacts with MSI-like histone chaperones to maintain accessibility at fruit morphogenesis genes. The Crjag mutant shows reduced ATAC signal and H3K18ac, increased H3K27me3 and repression of the cell-cycle regulator CrAUR2.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: The work provides a mechanistic chain beyond an inverse correlation between a histone mark and expression: TF/chaperone complex, chromatin state, target genes and fruit phenotype. Target identification, genetics and pharmacological evidence should be considered together.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: This is a useful model for interpreting pepper K5/K8 H3K27me3 clusters and prioritizing candidates with coordinated TF footprints, ATAC, H3K27me3 and expression changes.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: Research proposal: intersect candidate TF target regions with dynamic chromatin regions and prioritize concordant changes across layers for functional tests. The transferable element is the evidence framework, not an assumption that the same mechanism already operates in pepper.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: The system is Capsella rubella fruit shape, which differs from pepper ripening in both species and developmental process. Cross-species relevance requires independent validation, and omics intersections do not replace direct regulatory evidence.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: Examine how CrJAG direct targets are intersected with ATAC-seq and how pharmacological and genetic tests strengthen the omics associations.

evidence.abstract: The AP2/ERF transcription factor family is one of the largest transcription factor families in plants and plays essential roles in growth and development. Chili pepper, as a representative member of the Solanaceae family, is an important vegetable crop with enormous economic value. In this study, using the recently released gap-free telomere-to-telomere genome assembly of pepper, we re-annotated the AP2/ERF transcription factor family and identified 155 high-confidence members. Phylogenetic analysis classified these genes into five subfamilies: AP2 (19), ERF (82), DREB (51), RAV (1), and Soloist (2). Comprehensive analyses of gene structure, conserved motifs, chromosomal distribution, collinearity, cis-elements, and expression profiles revealed substantial structural conservation and functional diversification within the family. Expression profiling highlighted CaBBM, a key member of the AP2 subfamily, as a candidate developmental regulator, prompting further functional characterization. Expression analyses using qRT-PCR and promoter-GUS assays showed that CaBBM was preferentially expressed in stamens, while subcellular localization assays confirmed its nuclear localization. Preliminary analysis of biological functions suggests that heterologous expression of CaBBM in Arabidopsis can lead to phenotypes such as shorter primary roots, smaller leaves and floral organs, and decreased pollen number. In addition, yeast two-hybrid screening identified 12 candidate interacting proteins. These results provide a comprehensive framework for understanding the AP2/ERF family in chili pepper and lay a foundation for elucidating the function and regulatory mechanisms of CaBBM.

evidence.abstract: Key messageThis review synthesizes the molecular mechanisms of cold tolerance in pepper, integrating multi-omics data,genome editing, and precision breeding strategies to accelerate the development of cold-resilient cultivars. Cold stress is a significant environmental factor that affects the growth, productivity, and fruit quality of Capsicum annuum by impairing membrane integrity photosynthesis and cellular redox homeostasis. Although pepper has several endogenous cold-responsive regulators such as CaNAC035 and CabHLH035, along with antioxidant defense systems, its cold tolerance remains limited due to low transcriptional activation of key regulators, functional redundancy among cold-responsive genes, and the polygenicity of cold tolerance. These complexities, combined with low genetic diversity and linkage drag, have hindered the improvement of cold-resistant cultivars through conventional breeding. This review brings together the recent progress in understanding the molecular mechanisms of cold stress perception, signal transduction, transcriptional regulation, metabolic reprogramming, and phytohormone interactions in pepper. Precision Breeding 2.0 is a new innovation that combines the integration of multi-omics-based target identification with next-generation genome-editing techniques, allowing precise and multiplex engineering of complex and interconnected regulatory networks instead of single genes. We cover new approaches such as engineering the DREB/CBF pathway, allele-specific editing and targeted disruption of negative regulators to enhance the pathway(s) involved in cold response. Moreover, we propose a roadmap for integration of transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, high-throughput phenomics, and speed breeding to accelerate the identification, validation, and deployment of superior alleles to boost cold tolerance. This review provides a foundation for developing climate-resilient pepper cultivars by connecting functional genomics with precision genome engineering approaches to maintain productivity under variable environmental conditions.

evidence.abstract: Phytomelatonin has long been viewed as a pleiotropic stress signal that protects plants by scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS), reinforcing antioxidant capacity, and coordinating hormonal responses. That view remains correct, but it is no longer sufficient. Recent work indicates that phytomelatonin also shapes the regulatory architecture that determines whether stress-responsive genes are accessible, whether transcripts are processed and translated efficiently, and whether stress-induced states can persist after the initial stimulus has disappeared. Here, we synthesize four emerging layers of phytomelatonin action: DNA methylation and histone modifications, noncoding RNA (ncRNA) networks, N6 methyladenosine (m6A) RNA methylation and stress memory with potential transgenerational effects. Rather than listing stress phenotypes, we emphasize regulatory logic. Phytomelatonin can buffer stress induced DNA methylation shifts, modulate histone acetylation and methylation marks, rewire microRNA (miRNA), long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) networks and counteract cadmium-induced m6A hypermethylation. Its involvement in circular RNA (circRNA) regulation remains a testable hypothesis. These layers are likely integrated through redox status, hormone crosstalk, RNA stability, chromatin accessibility and DNA repair. We propose that phytomelatonin functions as an epigenetic and epitranscriptomic trigger capable of converting transient stress perception into durable transcriptional competence. Finally, we outline how single-cell multi-omics, targeted epigenome editing, epitranscriptomic profiling and field-scale validation of priming strategies can transform this conceptual framework into testable mechanisms and crop-improvement strategies.

evidence.abstract: The RNA polymerase II C-terminal domain (CTD) phosphatase CPL1/FRY2 is a multifunctional regulator involved in diverse stress responses, yet its role in orchestrating hormone-mediated immunity remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that CPL1 regulates ABA biosynthesis and modulates SA/JA-associated defence responses in Arabidopsis thaliana. Loss of CPL1 function compromises resistance to the hemibiotrophic bacterial pathogen Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 (Pst DC3000), coinciding with suppressed SA signalling and ectopic activation of JA-, ethylene-, and abscisic acid (ABA)-responsive genes. Hormone profiling revealed that upon Pst DC3000 infection, cpl1 mutants specifically accumulated ABA, but not SA, JA, or ethylene. Epistasis analyses showed that this ABA accumulation stems from the derepression of the seed-specific transcription factor FUSCA3 (FUS3) in vegetative tissues, which in turn drives expression of the ABA biosynthetic gene NCED3. Chromatin immunoprecipitation analyses further revealed that FUS3 silencing in wild-type plants is maintained by repressive epigenetic marks, including low histone acetylation and high H3K9me2/3 levels, modifications that are disrupted in cpl1 mutants. Consequently, CPL1 promotes resistance to biotrophic/hemibiotrophic pathogens by epigenetically silencing FUS3 to prevent pathogen-induced ABA biosynthesis, thereby modulating SA/JA-associated defence responses. Our findings position CPL1 as a key integrator of epigenetic regulation, hormone crosstalk, and pathogen-specific immune tuning.

evidence.abstract: Chilli (Capsicum annuum L.) is an economically important vegetable crop cultivated worldwide. Increasing drought stress associated with climate change has severely reduced chilli productivity. Although grafting and silicon-based nanomaterials have each been investigated independently as drought mitigation strategies in Solanaceae crops, this study represents, to our knowledge, the first investigation of their combined physiological, yield, and genome-wide transcriptomic effects in chilli under experimentally validated drought stress. Biodynamic nanosilica (BNS) is an α-quartz nanoparticle preparation (20-200 nm) derived from the biodynamic agricultural preparation BD501 through a vortex-triturating process, and distinct from chemically synthesised nanosilica in preparation method and surface bioavailability, applied as a foliar spray at 50 mg L-1. Five treatments were established: well-watered (WW), drought (D), grafting + BNS + drought (G+B+D), grafting + drought (G+D), and BNS + drought (B+D), each with three independent biological replicates. Under moderate-to-severe drought conditions (DSI 62-64%; VWC ~12% v/v at 14 days), the combined G+B+D treatment significantly improved plant height (3.05-fold over D), leaf relative water content (83% vs 49% in D), net photosynthetic rate (2.0-fold over D), water-use efficiency (+40%), and antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD: 3.1-fold; CAT: 2.8-fold over D), while reducing lipid peroxidation by 76%. Root architecture was also substantially enhanced, with a 4.1-fold increase in root length and a 3.1-fold increase in root surface area relative to D. Fruit yield increased by 79% relative to drought-stressed non-grafted plants. Transcriptomic analysis using Illumina NovaSeq 6000 identified 1,051 DEGs (431 upregulated, 620 downregulated; FDR 2FC| > 1). Integrated transcriptomic-phenotypic concordance analysis revealed enrichment of MAPK signalling, ABA-mediated regulation (including ABA binding and (+)-ABA 8'-hydroxylase activity), and phenylpropanoid biosynthesis as the enriched pathways. Protein-protein interaction network analysis further revealed coordinated regulation of redox homeostasis, drought-responsive hormone signalling, and water transport gene modules in the combined treatment. These findings demonstrate that integrating grafting with biodynamic nanosilica is a promising strategy to enhance drought resilience and productivity in chilli, offering a sustainable approach for vegetable production under drought.

sections.text: This review summarizes recent advances of CRISPR/Cas applications in Solanaceae crops such as tomato, potato, eggplant, and pepper, highlighting breakthroughs in precise modifications of genes for disease resistance, stress tolerance, and fruit quality regulation.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: It introduces emerging techniques like base editing, prime editing, and transgene-free RNP delivery, emphasizing expanded scope and precision in genome editing that enable modification of complex polygenic traits.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: Provides the latest genome editing tools and strategies for functional gene validation and breeding in pepper, especially for targeted improvement of fruit quality and resistance genes, facilitating integration with epigenomic data.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: The review suggests combining CRISPR editing with multi-omics to prioritize editing of fruit ripening key transcription factors marked by accessible chromatin and active epigenetic marks, accelerating functional validation and breeding.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: Current constraints include transformation efficiency and homologous recombination levels; regulatory concerns and potential off-target effects require caution; pepper-specific genetic backgrounds affecting editing are still under evaluation.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: Focus on emerging editing methods (e.g. prime editing), delivery technologies, and case studies integrating multi-omics data to enhance editing efficiency and precision in pepper.

evidence.abstract: Malnutrition and climate-induced stress remain major constraints to global food and nutritional security despite the yield gains of the Green Revolution. Solanaceae crops such as tomato, potato, brinjal, and pepper are key sources of vitamins, minerals, and bioactive compounds. Yet, their genetic improvement has been limited by narrow diversity and complex polygenic traits. The advent of CRISPR/Cas-mediated genome editing provides a transformative platform for precision crop improvement by enabling targeted modification of genes controlling stress tolerance, yield, and nutritional quality. In Solanaceae, CRISPR/Cas applications have successfully enhanced resistance against major pathogens (SlMlo1, SlPelo, SlDCL2), improved abiotic stress tolerance through editing of SlMAPK3, SlCBF1, and SlBZR1, and optimized fruit quality traits via modulation of Psy1, CrtR-b2, and fiAD2/3. Emerging innovations, such as base and prime editing, and RNP-mediated transgene-free delivery, are expanding the precision and scope of editing. However, challenges persist, including genotype-dependent transformation, low HDR efficiency, and incomplete understanding of off-target and epigenetic effects. Integrating CRISPR with omics-guided gene discovery, efficient transformation systems, and regulatory harmonization can accelerate the development of nutritionally enriched, stress-resilient, and sustainable Solanaceae varieties. This review synthesizes recent advances, identifies critical limitations, and outlines future opportunities for deploying CRISPR/Cas technology to achieve next-generation breeding and food system resilience.

en.heading: Calcium Sources Mitigate Salt Stress and Improve the Physiological and Productive Performance of Bell Peppers

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: This study compares substrate and foliar calcium application methods and different calcium sources (none, calcium nitrate, calcium complexed with amino acids) for alleviating salt stress in pepper, finding that amino acid-complexed calcium significantly enhances photosystem II efficiency, stomatal conductance, fruit yield, and reduces apical rot.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: Assessment of gas exchange parameters and chlorophyll fluorescence elucidated the improvement of photosynthetic function and stability of chlorophyll indices by calcium sources, thereby mitigating salt stress effects.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: Provides experimental evidence and treatment strategies relevant for pepper salt stress physiology and fruit quality studies, complementing multi-omics analysis of photosynthesis and redox-related gene epigenetic regulation in the 22-tissue atlas.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: Suggests calcium nutrition forms and application methods markedly affect physiological status and gene expression in leaf photosynthetic tissues, inviting integration with ATAC-seq and histone modification data for deeper understanding of salt stress regulatory networks.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: Experiments were conducted in substrate hydroponic systems, so extension to soil-based production requires caution. Salt stress levels and long-term safety of amino acid-complexed calcium require further validation.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: Focus on relationships between photosystem II efficiency, stomatal conductance, salt stress-related genes’ chromatin accessibility and histone activation marks.

evidence.abstract: Bell peppers (Capsicum annuum L.) are of great importance and have high productive potential in Brazil, especially in the Northeast region; however, their production is limited due to salinity problems in water and soil. The objective of this study was to evaluate sources and methods of calcium application for mitigating salt stress in bell pepper plants grown in a substrate-based hydroponic system. The experiment was conducted using a split-plot design in a 2 × 2 × 3 layout with four replicates, consisting of two application methods (substrate and spray), two ECiw levels (0.5 and 5.0 dS m-1), and three calcium sources (no calcium-NCa; calcium nitrate-Ca(NO3)2; calcium complexed with amino acids-Ca-AA). Forty-two days after transplanting, gas exchange analysis, chlorophyll a, b, and total chlorophyll indices, chlorophyll fluorescence, fruit number and weight, and yield per plant were measured. Ca-AA showed higher photosystem II efficiency when applied via the substrate and higher stomatal conductance (28.10%), resulted in higher fruit yield compared to the other treatments, and contributed to a reduction in apical rot. Meanwhile, the application of Ca(NO3)2 improved electron transport in photosystem II by 5.46%, gas exchange, and increased chlorophyll b and total chlorophyll indices by 29.62% and 10.93%, respectively. It is concluded that the application of Ca sources, especially Ca-AA, has the potential to mitigate the effects of salt stress on bell pepper plants in a substrate-based hydroponic system, improving their photosynthetic and productive performance.

en.heading: CgMYC2 directly activates jasmonate-induced naringin biosynthesis in Citrus grandis 'Tomentosa'

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: This study identified CgMYC2 as a core jasmonate-responsive transcription activator in citrus, directly binding and activating promoters of flavonoid biosynthetic genes, significantly increasing bitter flavonoid content.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: Utilizing Pull-down, Co-IP, EMSA, dual-luciferase assays, VIGS, and CUT&Tag, the research established the direct binding of MYC2 to JAZ and downstream target genes, clarifying the regulatory cascade.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: MYC2 family is conserved jasmonate pathway transcription factor broadly present in pepper; insights on regulation of fruit quality and secondary metabolites bear relevance.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: Highlights MYC2 binding to G-box motifs as key jasmonate regulatory mechanism, suggesting integration with ATAC-seq and histone mark data in the 22-tissue atlas to unravel fruit ripening transcriptional control.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: No direct functional validation in pepper and metabolic differences between citrus and Solanaceae necessitate cautious extrapolation.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: Focus on MYC2-mediated G-box dependent promoter binding and transcriptional activation mechanisms, and its regulatory network during fruit ripening and hormone signaling.

evidence.abstract: Key messageCgMYC2 links jasmonate signaling to naringin biosynthesis by binding G-box motifs and activating flavonoid-pathway promoters in Citrus grandis 'Tomentosa' Naringin, the predominant bitter-flavanone glycoside in Citrus grandis 'Tomentosa', has well-characterized biosynthetic enzymes, yet the transcriptional regulators coupling hormonal signals to pathway activation remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that CgMYC2, a jasmonate-responsive bHLH transcription factor, functions as a central activator of naringin biosynthesis. Exogenous methyl jasmonate (MeJA) treatment increased naringin content 3.45-fold in seedlings, coinciding with a rapid 6.6-fold induction of CgMYC2 that preceded the peak transcription of five core biosynthetic genes (CgPAL5, CgCHS, CgFNS, Cg7GlcT, and Cg1,2RhaT). Physical interaction between CgMYC2 and the JAZ protein CgJAZ3 was confirmed by pull-down and Co-IP assays, placing CgMYC2 within the canonical jasmonate signaling cascade. Y1H confirmed CgMYC2 binding to the Cg1,2RhaT promoter, EMSA demonstrated direct G-box-dependent binding to all five pathway promoters, and dual-luciferase assays showed transactivation of all five promoters, with the strongest activation for CgCHS. As complementary chromatin-level support, a single-sample CUT&Tag profile revealed G-box-enriched CgMYC2-associated chromatin regions across jasmonate-responsive and secondary-metabolic loci. Virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) of CgMYC2 reduced naringin content by ~21% and suppressed biosynthetic gene expression, supporting its positive contribution. Furthermore, heterologous overexpression in tomato activated the flavonoid pathway and elevated 16 flavonoid compounds, consistent with evolutionary conservation of the MYC2-G-box regulatory logic. These findings establish CgMYC2 as a central, JA-responsive activator bridging jasmonate perception and naringin biosynthesis, providing a molecular framework for the targeted improvement of bitter-flavonoid traits in citrus.

en.heading: Epi-PoreC: a nanopore-based method for simultaneous profiling of chromatin conformation, DNA methylation, and chromatin accessibility

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: Epi-PoreC technology enables simultaneous nanopore sequencing-based detection of chromatin conformation capture, exogenous adenine methylation marking of accessible chromatin, and endogenous cytosine methylation, providing single-molecule integrated analysis of 3D genome and epigenetics.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: Combining PoreC and Fiber-seq methods, detecting 6-methyladenine and 5-methylcytosine on DNA molecules enables high-throughput consistent assessment of chromatin 3D spatial organization and epigenetic status.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: Offers a future technical solution for integrated 3D genome, methylation, and accessibility multi-omics in pepper, fostering deeper functional chromatin analysis for the 22-tissue atlas.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: Can expand pepper multi-omics atlas by capturing chromatin structure, DNA methylation and openness at single-molecule resolution, aiding identification of regulatory elements and distal enhancer function.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: Validated only in Arabidopsis; adaptation challenges remain due to plant cell wall complexity and genome size differences in pepper.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: Focus on Epi-PoreC methodological principles, data analysis workflows and comparative advantages over standard PoreC and Fiber-seq, laying groundwork for integrative pepper multi-omics.

evidence.abstract: Understanding how the three-dimensional (3D) organization of the genome relates to chromatin and epigenetic landscapes requires methods capable of measuring chromosomal DNA interactions and chromatin modifications in an integrated manner. Current approaches typically use separate assays to assess chromatin conformation and epigenetic state, thus these features are not assessed on the same DNA molecules. Here, we describe Epi-PoreC, an Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing-based method that combines the chromosome conformation capture method, PoreC with Fiber-seq, a method for detecting accessible chromatin regions based on their ability to be labeled using an exogenous adenosine methyltransferase. The positions of chromosome contacts, 6-methyladenosines, and endogenous 5-methylcytosines are then detected by nanopore sequencing, all on the same DNA molecules. Using Arabidopsis thaliana nuclei, we demonstrate that Epi-PoreC yields genome-wide chromatin contact maps comparable to those obtained by standard PoreC and DNA methylation and accessibility profiles comparable to standard Fiber-seq experiments. Epi-PoreC is thus an efficient means for conducting epigenetic and 3D genome profiling on individual DNA sequences in a single assay.

en.heading: Pepper preprint proposes that DOF factors suppress GGPPS1 and precursor supply, limiting fruit capsanthin accumulation

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: The preprint reports that dynamic chromatin states and accessibility during pepper fruit color transition were used to map upstream TF footprints of capsanthin-biosynthesis genes; stable overexpression experiments further nominated two DOF factors as negative regulators of capsanthin accumulation. The abstract also states that both factors repress GGPPS1 expression and lower in vivo GGPP content, suggesting that restriction of carotenoid precursor supply may be part of their action.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: The study combines chromatin-accessibility information from pericarp during color transition with transcription-factor footprints, then tests candidate factors by stable overexpression in pepper; the abstract does not specify the accessibility-sequencing platform or footprint algorithm, nor does it provide details of independent validation that the footprints represent direct binding. The results support an association between DOF overexpression and changes in GGPPS1 expression, GGPP, and capsanthin, but the specific molecular mechanism should be judged cautiously in light of the full evidence.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: The study's crop, tissue, and trait directly match pepper fruit ripening and pigment accumulation, and it offers candidate negative regulators for a capsanthin-related TF network. Because this is a preprint and the abstract does not provide candidate gene identifiers, cultivar background, or effect sizes, the candidate nodes and regulatory directions still require independent validation.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: Research implication: use RNA-seq across the 22 tissues to locate carotenoid-pathway genes and candidate DOF factors with high expression during fruit ripening, then integrate them with ATAC-seq accessible regions, CUT&Tag profiles for H3K4me1/H3K4me3/H3K27ac/H3K27me3, and WGBS methylation states to prioritize tissue- or ripening-stage-specific candidate relationships. The candidates could be incorporated into the fruit-ripening TF network, with regions near GGPPS1 prioritized for testing; these multi-omics correspondences are not established by the abstract and remain to be tested.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: This is a preprint, so its conclusions have not yet been confirmed through journal peer review; neither a footprint map nor an overexpression phenotype alone proves direct binding under endogenous conditions or a complete causal chain. The abstract provides no data on performance across varieties, field stability, fruit-quality tradeoffs, or editing feasibility.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: First examine how chromatin accessibility and footprints were constructed across color-transition stages, the evidence from overexpressing the two DOF factors, and the experimental relationships among GGPPS1 expression, GGPP, and capsanthin. Then assess direct-binding evidence and genetic-background information for the candidate TFs; this digest is based on the abstract and has not reviewed the full text, figures, or supplementary materials.

evidence.abstract: Abstract  Capsanthin is a rare, oxygenated carotenoid of high nutritional and industrial value, which rapidly accumulates as pepper fruit ripens, resulting in the transition of color from green to red. evidence.abstract: Salt stress severely limits crop growth and productivity, particularly in horticultural crops. Cysteine-rich receptor-like kinases (CRKs) are important membrane-associated signaling proteins involved in plant environmental responses; however, their functions in salt stress adaptation in Solanaceae crops remain limited. In this study, a genome-wide identification and comparative analysis of the CRK gene family was performed in pepper (Capsicum annuum), eggplant (Solanum melongena), and tomato (Solanum lycopersicum). 37 CRK genes were identified in pepper. Comprehensive analyses, including phylogenetic relationships, conserved domain organization, motif composition, and evolutionary patterns, demonstrated that CRK proteins in Solanaceae share highly conserved structural characteristics, consisting of extracellular DUF26 domains, transmembrane regions, and intracellular serine/threonine kinase domains. Expression analysis revealed that multiple CRK genes responded to salt stress, among which CaCRK10 showed strong induction and was selected for functional characterization. Subcellular localization analysis indicated that CaCRK10 was mainly localized to the plasma membrane. Overexpression of CaCRK10 improved the salt tolerance of pepper plants, as indicated by stronger antioxidant activity and lower malondialdehyde accumulation under salt stress. The transgenic plants also showed a better balance between K+ and Na+, together with improved osmotic adjustment. In addition, CaCRK10 overexpression increased the transcript levels of several SOS- and NHX-related genes associated with ion homeostasis. A similar response was observed for the eggplant homolog SmCRK6, whose expression was strongly induced by salt treatment. Its overexpression also contributed to improved salt tolerance, which was associated with changes in antioxidant defense, ion homeostasis, and osmotic regulation. Together, these findings initially revealed that CRK members play conserved positive regulatory roles in salt stress adaptation in Solanaceae crops and provide potential genetic resources for molecular breeding of salt-tolerant varieties.

evidence.abstract: Auxin is a fundamental phytohormone that orchestrates developmental processes in plants. Flavin monooxygenase (YUCCA) serves as the rate-limiting enzyme in the indole-3-pyruvic acid pathway (IPA) pathway, and its main function is to convert IPA into IAA. In this study, 12 members of the MiYUCCA gene family were mined and identified from the genomic data of mango (Mangifera indica). Phylogenetic tree analysis classified mango YUCCA into five categories. Cis-elements analysis of the promoter indicated that the promoter region contained a large number of hormone response elements and abiotic elements. Expression analysis revealed that the majority of MiYUCCA gene family members displayed high expression abundance at the early developmental stages of fruits, and their expression decreased or even remained unexpressed with the fruit growth and development. MiYUCCA10A and MiYUCCA10B were selected for functional verification. Overexpression of MiYUCCA10A and MiYUCCA10B promoted the early flowering in transgenic Arabidopsis and tomato, enhanced the salt and drought resistance, and also increased the content of IAA in transgenic plants. In addition, MiYUCCA10A and MiYUCCA10B significantly reduced the seed number of transgenic Arabidopsis and tomato plants, exerted no effect on the pod length of Arabidopsis, but markedly decreased the fruit size of tomato. The interaction of MiYUCCA10A/B with the SHORT VEGETATIVE PHASE 1/2/3/4/5 (MiSVP1/2/3/4/5) and FLOWERING LOCUS C (MiFLC) was revealed using both yeast two-hybrid (Y2H) and bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) analyses. These results indicate that the MiYUCCA10A/B were not only involved in flowering, but also related to stress tolerance and fruit development.

evidence.abstract: Fruit firmness is a critical quality trait primarily governed by the structure and composition of the cell wall. While extensive research has focused on firmness dynamics during fruit ripening, the regulatory mechanisms governing its establishment during early fruit development remain poorly understood. Previous studies have demonstrated that VASCULAR SPECIFICITY FACTOR 1 (VSF-1), a member of the bZIP family, is activated in vitro by the key fruit softening regulator LOB1, suggesting its potential role in the regulation of fruit firmness. In this study, we generated both CRISPR-Cas9-mediated knockout and overexpression lines in tomato; functional analysis revealed that the loss of VSF-1 function reduced fruit firmness, whereas its overexpression enhanced it, thereby establishing VSF-1 as a positive regulator of firmness. By integrating transcriptomic and DNA affinity purification sequencing profiling, we delineated the VSF-1-controlled gene regulatory network associated with cell wall remodeling and identified the β-galactosidase gene, TBG6, as a direct target. Our findings uncover a novel role for VSF-1 in the transcriptional regulation of tomato fruit texture, underscore the functional diversification within the Solanaceae bZIP subfamily I, and provide new insights into the genetic improvement of fruit quality.

evidence.abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H2S) and its mediated protein persulfidation regulate fruit ripening. Fruit aroma, a key quality trait formed during ripening, largely determines consumer preferences. However, the mechanism by which H2S modulates aroma biosynthesis in pear remains unclear. This study reveals that H2S inhibited aroma biosynthesis in 'Nanguo' pear and downregulated the fatty acid desaturase gene PuFAD8. Transient overexpression and silencing assays confirmed that PuFAD8 was required for linoleic acid synthesis, a key aroma precursor. Heterologous overexpression of PuFAD8 in tomato and its knockout in tomato further validated that PuFAD8 promoted fruit aroma formation, while H2S suppressed this function. Transcriptome analysis identified transcription factors PuMYB21 and PuERF106 co-expressed with PuFAD8. Dual-luciferase and yeast one-hybrid assays revealed that PuMYB21 bound and activated the PuFAD8 promoter. Moreover, Y2H, luciferase complementation, pull-down, and transient expression assays demonstrated that PuERF106 interacted with PuMYB21, synergistically enhancing aroma biosynthesis. Persulfidation at Cys162 of PuERF106 attenuated its interaction with PuMYB21, thereby inhibiting aromatic compound synthesis in pear fruit. Subsequently, the biological function of the PuERF106-PuMYB21-PuFAD8 molecular module was validated using stable transgenic pear callus lines and a panel of heterologous and endogenous transgenic tomato lines. This study reveals a novel regulatory mechanism where H2S-mediated persulfidation suppresses pear aroma biosynthesis, providing a theoretical basis for genetic improvement of high-quality pear.

evidence.abstract: Key messagePpAPRR2 promotes chlorophyll accumulation in peach fruit, and its overexpression enhances fruitgreening in tomato. Fruit peel color represents an important quality trait in peach (Prunus persica L.), determined by the dynamic balance between chlorophyll and anthocyanin metabolism. While the regulatory networks controlling anthocyanin regulation have been well documented, the molecular mechanisms governing chlorophyll accumulation and peel greening remain less understood. Here, we identified nine ARR-B family transcription factors in peach and found that PpAPRR2 was predominantly expressed during early fruit development, showing a strong positive correlation with chlorophyll levels. Subcellular localization assays revealed that PpAPRR2 was localized in the nucleus. In contrast, heterologous overexpression of PpAPRR2 in tomato resulted in darker green fruits, enhanced chlorophyll content, and increased expression of chlorophyll biosynthesis genes. Transcriptome analysis further confirmed promotion of photosynthetic pathways and suppression of chlorophyll degradation in PpAPRR2-overexpressing tomato fruits. Together, these results demonstrate that PpAPRR2 acts as a regulator promoting chlorophyll accumulation and chloroplast development in peach fruit. This study provides novel insights into the genetic control of fruit peel coloration and offers a potential molecular target for improving fruit quality through genetic engineering.

evidence.abstract: Studying the functions of the UV-B photoreceptor UVR8 in large, indeterminate-growth tomato plants is challenging due to the difficulty of applying uniform UV-B irradiation. To overcome this limitation, we generated a constitutively active photoreceptor variant, SlUVR8W289A, by substituting tryptophan 289 with alanine. Notably, SlUVR8W289A failed to activate UV-B-induced early transcriptional responses in seedlings. In mature plants, SlUVR8W289A significantly increased chlorophyll accumulation in fruits by regulating key genes involved in chlorophyll biosynthesis. Collectively, our results demonstrate that SlUVR8W289A represents a constitutively active UVR8 photoreceptor for long-term UV-B responses, allowing the dissection of UV-B signaling pathways independently of UV-B exposure. This study establishes intrinsic UV-B signaling as a critical regulator of seedling establishment, fruit development, and stress adaptation in tomato. Our findings provide a mechanistic basis for harnessing UV-B signaling to improve horticultural crop performance, and position SlUVR8W289A as a valuable genetic tool for both fundamental UV-B research and practical crop improvement.

evidence.abstract: Cold stress severely restricts the geographical distribution and productivity of Camellia sinensis (tea plant). Although the plant cuticle wax serves as a critical barrier in resisting both biotic and abiotic stresses, its epigenetic regulation during cold stress remains poorly understood. Here, we show that exogenous arginine alleviates cold-induced damage by increasing cuticle thickness, and enhancing the accumulation of very-long-chain fatty acids and alkanes. Transcriptome-based weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified CsKCS3 as a key regulator of wax biosynthesis. Virus-induced gene silencing in tea plants and heterologous overexpression in Arabidopsis thaliana demonstrated that CsKCS3 positively regulates fatty acid biosynthesis and contributes to cold tolerance. Furthermore, the trimethylation of histone H3 at Lysine 4 (H3K4me3) is increased during arginine-induced processes and enhances the expression of the CsSDG36 and CsKCS3. Further, we identified that CsSDG36 encodes an H3K4 methyltransferase. Arginine treatment mitigated cold damage in CsSDG36-silenced tea plants, which was associated with recovery of CsKCS3 expression. Mechanistically, CsSDG36 enhanced H3K4me3 enrichment at the promoter and exon regions of CsKCS3, thereby activating CsKCS3 transcription. These findings reveal a CsSDG36-H3K4me3-CsKCS3 regulatory module through which arginine promotes cuticular wax accumulation and cold tolerance in tea plants. These findings uncover a novel epigenetic circuitry in which exogenous arginine regulates chromatin remodeling to structurally fortify the epidermal lipid barrier, offering a vital conceptual framework for breeding climate-resilient perennial crops.

Biochemical, transcriptomic, and transcriptional activity analyses confirmed the functional restoration of SlGLK2 in the CR-Slglk2-4 line. This study not only provides a useful Micro-Tom line for investigating plastid biogenesis in tomato fruit but also demonstrates the potential of genome editing to restore the latent functions of pseudogenized genes in modern crops, offering a new approach for recovering traits lost during plant domestication or crop improvement.

papers.heading: [补录]中度水分亏缺通过SlNAP2转录网络提高番茄果实营养品质

sections.label: 真正的新发现
sections.text: 补录：番茄中度水分亏缺与多种类胡萝卜素、可溶性固形物、可溶性蛋白和抗坏血酸增加相关，作者报告其试验条件下产量无显著下降。SlNAP2敲除降低果实营养品质，过表达在中度水分亏缺下提高品质，支持其参与该处理下的品质响应。

sections.label: 机制或方法上的关键点
sections.text: 研究报告SlNAP2直接结合并激活番茄番茄红素合成基因SlPSY2、SlPDS、SlZDS及抗坏血酸合成基因SlGMP、SlGGP的启动子；水分亏缺增强了这一转录激活。摘要还称这五个下游基因的功能分析支持其介导SlNAP2相关代谢物积累。

sections.label: 与你的辣椒研究关系
sections.text: 番茄与辣椒均为茄科果实作物，该研究提供了可供辣椒检验的“水分条件—TF—代谢基因—营养性状”框架。摘要没有提供辣椒中SlNAP2对应基因的同源、旁系同源、结合或遗传功能证据，也不能据此断言辣椒在相同水分处理下会有相同产量与品质反应。

sections.label: 对22组织图谱的具体启示
sections.text: 研究启示：在辣椒22组织RNA-seq中关注NAP类TF及类胡萝卜素、抗坏血酸通路基因的组织与果实阶段表达；将候选TF与ATAC-seq和四种CUT&Tag标记整合以筛选可能的活性启动子，并用WGBS评估相关区域甲基化。若要构建成熟TF网络，应把水分处理作为独立条件，检验网络边是否随处理变化，而非把共表达当作直接结合证据。

sections.label: 需要注意
sections.text: 摘要中的“产量无显著下降”仅限于其试验条件；没有据此证明其他水分强度、遗传背景或田间环境中无产量代价。转录因子直接结合的证据来自番茄，向辣椒迁移仍须验证，且本研究并未测量染色质可及性或组蛋白标记。

sections.label: 建议优先看
sections.text: 优先看水分处理与品质测定条件、SlNAP2敲除和过表达的结果，以及SlNAP2对五个启动子的结合和激活证据。再核对下游基因功能分析如何支持类胡萝卜素和抗坏血酸变化。

en.heading: [Backfill] Moderate water deficit improves tomato fruit nutritional quality through the SlNAP2 transcriptional network

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: Backfill: In tomato, moderate water deficit was associated with increases in several carotenoids, soluble solids, soluble protein, and ascorbic acid; the authors report no significant yield reduction under their experimental conditions. sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: The study reports that SlNAP2 directly binds and activates the promoters of the tomato lycopene-biosynthesis genes SlPSY2, SlPDS, and SlZDS, and the ascorbic-acid-biosynthesis genes SlGMP and SlGGP; water deficit enhanced this transcriptional activation. The abstract also states that functional analyses of these five downstream genes support their mediation of SlNAP2-associated metabolite accumulation.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: Tomato and pepper are both Solanaceae fruit crops, and this study provides a framework for testing in pepper: “water status–TF–metabolic genes–nutritional traits.” The abstract provides no evidence for orthology, paralogy, binding, or genetic function of the corresponding pepper gene, and does not establish that pepper would show the same yield and quality responses under the same water treatment.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: Research implication: track NAP-family TFs and carotenoid- and ascorbic-acid-pathway genes across tissues and fruit stages in the 22-tissue pepper RNA-seq atlas; integrate candidate TFs with ATAC-seq and the four CUT&Tag marks to prioritize potentially active promoters, and use WGBS to assess methylation in relevant regions. To build a ripening TF network, treat water status as a separate condition and test whether network edges vary with treatment rather than treating co-expression as evidence of direct binding.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: The abstract's report of “no significant yield reduction” applies only to its experimental conditions; it does not establish the absence of yield costs at other water-deficit levels, in other genetic backgrounds, or in field environments. Evidence for direct TF binding comes from tomato and still requires validation before transfer to pepper; this study did not measure chromatin accessibility or histone marks.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: First inspect the water-treatment and quality-assessment conditions, results from SlNAP2 knockout and overexpression, and evidence for SlNAP2 binding to and activating the five promoters. evidence.abstract: Moderate water deficit is an effective strategy to improve fruit nutritional quality, yet the underlying molecular mechanism remains largely elusive, limiting its application in high-quality crop cultivation. Here, we report that moderate water deficit simultaneously elevates the contents of α-carotene, β-carotene, lutein, lycopene, soluble solids, soluble protein, and ascorbic acid in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.) fruits, with no significant reduction in fruit yield under our experimental conditions. Through transcriptome analysis and RT-qPCR, we identified SlNAP2 as a central transcription factor regulating this process. Moderate water deficit upregulates SlNAP2 expression. Knockout of SlNAP2 significantly reduces fruit nutritional quality, whereas its overexpression enhances it under moderate water deficit. Importantly, moderate water deficit promotes the improvement of tomato fruit nutritional quality in a SlNAP2-dependent manner. We further demonstrate that SlNAP2 directly binds to and activates the promoters of key lycopene biosynthesis genes (SlPSY2, SlPDS, SlZDS) and ascorbic acid biosynthesis genes (SlGMP, SlGGP), and that moderate water deficit enhances this transcriptional activation. Functional analyses further support the role of these five genes as downstream effectors that mediate SlNAP2-dependent lycopene and ascorbic acid accumulation. Collectively, our findings reveal that moderate water deficit enhances tomato fruit nutritional quality by boosting SlNAP2-mediated transcriptional activation of lycopene and ascorbate biosynthesis, establishing SlNAP2 as a central regulator linking water deficit to fruit quality and providing mechanistic insights into stress-promoted metabolite accumulation.

en.heading: [Backfill] Heterologous overexpression of ChCAX3 delays tomato coloration and softening, suggesting potential for fruit-ripening regulation

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: Backfill: The abstract reports that overexpression of the Cerasus humilis vacuolar cation/H+ exchanger ChCAX3 in tomato increased fruit calcium content, delayed coloration, reduced softening, and extended the ripening period by approximately 14 days. Yeast complementation and Arabidopsis assays support its calcium-transport activity, while the cross-species test of fruit-ripening phenotypes was conducted by overexpression in tomato.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: The study proposes that ChCAX3-mediated vacuolar calcium sequestration may alter cytosolic Ca2+ homeostasis and is accompanied by changes in the expression of genes related to ethylene biosynthesis and cell-wall degradation; the abstract describes a possible effect on the ChCBL10–ChCIPK3 module. Some links in this mechanism remain proposed, and the abstract provides no direct chromatin-regulation evidence in pepper or tomato.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: The heterologous overexpression result in tomato makes this study a testable reference for pepper ripening, fruit firmness, and postharvest quality. Orthology of the Cerasus humilis candidate in pepper, functional conservation, and the specific effects of changing calcium allocation in pepper fruit have not been established.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: Research implication: compare CAX-family candidates with ethylene-biosynthesis and cell-wall-degradation gene expression across pepper fruit-ripening stages in the 22-tissue RNA-seq atlas, while distinguishing fruit samples from flowers, leaves, and other tissues. ATAC-seq, the four CUT&Tag marks, and WGBS could test whether candidate regulatory regions in the ripening TF network change across stages; the original study did not perform these epigenomic assays, so they should not be presumed to cause ripening differences.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: The abstract reports an approximately 14-day extension of the ripening period but gives no pepper results, stability across varieties, or postharvest storage conditions, so commercial shelf-life gains cannot be estimated directly. Several links from calcium homeostasis to ethylene and cell-wall changes are described as possible mechanisms and should not be presented as a fully established causal chain.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: First inspect the tomato overexpression results for coloration, firmness, calcium content, and ripening period, followed by the yeast complementation and Arabidopsis calcium-transport validation. Keep the reported experimental observations distinct from the proposed mechanism involving the Ca2+ signaling module.

evidence.abstract: Cerasus humilis is a calcium-rich fruit crop with high nutritional value, but its synchronized ripening causes concentrated harvest and short shelf life. In this study, ChCAX3, a vacuolar cation/H+ exchanger, was identified as a key regulator of fruit ripening. ChCAX3 showed high expression in fruit and stem tissues and was upregulated by CaCl2 and ethephon treatments. however, repressed during fruit ripening by ChMYB16. Yeast complementation and Arabidopsis thaliana assays validated its Ca2+ transport activity. Overexpression of ChCAX3 in tomato increased fruit Ca2+ content, delayed coloration, reduced softening, and extended the ripening period by approximately 14 days. ChCAX3-mediated vacuolar Ca2+ sequestration may maintain low cytosolic Ca2+ levels, thereby potentially attenuate the expression and activity of a presumptive Ca2+ sensor ChCBL10 and its interacting kinase ChCIPK3 at the vacuolar membrane. This attenuation of the ChCBL10-ChCIPK3 module was accompanied by reduced expression of ethylene biosynthesis genes (ChACS1, ChACO1) and cell wall degradation-related genes (ChPG1, ChPG2), which may collectively delay the ethylene burst and preserving fruit firmness. Conversely, repression of ChCAX3 by ChMYB16 during late ripening may elevate cytosolic Ca2+, potentially activate the ChCBL10-ChCIPK3 signaling cascade, and accelerated senescence. Overall, these findings demonstrated that ChCAX3 positively regulates Ca2+ accumulation and delays fruit ripening via Ca2+ signaling-mediated modulation of ethylene pathways, providing new insights into Ca2+-hormone crosstalk in fruit physiology and identifying a potential target for extending shelf life and enhancing nutritional quality.

en.heading: [Backfill] A GhEBS1 structural variant is associated with larger cotton bolls and promotes fruit enlargement in heterologous tomato expression

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: Backfill: Map-based cloning identified cotton GhEBS1 as a positive regulator of boll size, and the abstract reports that an 845-bp structural variant in a promoter-proximal intron is associated with differences in local chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and expression. The abstract also reports that overexpression or heterologous expression of GhEBS1 in cotton, tomato, and Arabidopsis promoted enlargement of the corresponding fruits or organs; breeding evaluations associated the elite allele with increased boll size, seed size, and boll weight.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: The abstract describes interactions of GhEBS1 with GhPPD1/2 and GhKIX8/9, and an association with downstream cell-proliferation-related genes and changes in cell number; the structural-variant-associated modifications include H3K27 and H3K9 methylation levels and acetylation. The specific chromatin-assay methods and corresponding regulatory relationships in pepper are not provided in the abstract, so this association cannot be described as a mechanism validated in pepper.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: The heterologous expression result in tomato makes this a Solanaceae reference for fruit-size research, but the core genetic discovery and breeding evaluation are from cotton. Whether pepper has functionally corresponding EBS1, PPD, or KIX members, whether allelic variation affects fruit size, and whether there are quality or yield costs remain to be tested.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: Research implication: use RNA-seq across the 22 tissues to identify candidate cell-proliferation TF networks expressed during fruit expansion, then compare candidate regulatory-region states using ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag for H3K4me1/H3K4me3/H3K27ac/H3K27me3, and WGBS. Structural variants could be included as genetic variables when interpreting local accessibility and expression differences; the paper's abstract provides no pepper data and does not specify a directly reusable chromatin-sequencing workflow.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: The association among a structural variant, local chromatin, expression, and size traits in cotton, together with heterologous expression in tomato, does not demonstrate that the same gene network is conserved or has the same effect in pepper. The abstract provides no fruit-size evidence in pepper; any pepper editing or improvement proposal is an extrapolation that remains to be tested.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: First inspect the evidence linking the 845-bp variant to GhEBS1 expression, chromatin features, and cotton-boll phenotype, along with the tomato heterologous-expression and GhEBS1 protein-interaction results. Then check the chromatin-assay methods and the background used to evaluate the elite allele, which are not specified in the abstract.

evidence.abstract: Fruit size is not only a crucial fitness trait in plant evolution but also an important agronomic target in crop domestication and improvement, yet its regulatory mechanisms remain poorly characterized. Here, we identified an F-box E3 ubiquitin ligase gene, GhEBS1 (ENLARGED BOLL SIZE 1), as a positive regulator of cotton boll size via map-based cloning. An 845-bp structural variant in the promoter-proximal intronic region of GhEBS1 alters local chromatin accessibility and histone modifications, specifically H3K27 and H3K9 methylation levels and acetylation, thereby modulating GhEBS1 expression and driving boll size divergence. Overexpression or heterologous expression of GhEBS1 in cotton (capsule), tomato (berry) and Arabidopsis (silique) promoted fruit enlargement, indicating its functional conservation. Further analysis showed that GhEBS1 interacts with GhPPD1/2 and GhKIX8/9 to modulate downstream cell proliferation-related genes to control cell number and boll size. Breeding evaluations confirm that the elite GhEBS1L allele significantly increases boll size, seed size and boll weight. Haplotype analysis reveals that GhEBS1L originated from Gossypium hirsutum race latifolium and underwent artificial selection during cotton domestication. Our findings provide new insights into the regulation of plant fruit size and present a valuable genetic locus for crop yield improvement.

evidence.abstract: Cold stress severely restricts pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) growth and productivity by disrupting cellular homeostasis and inducing oxidative damage. Although HD-ZIP transcription factors play important roles in plant abiotic stress responses, the molecular mechanisms regulating their function during cold stress remain largely unknown. Here, we characterized the pepper HD-ZIP transcription factor CaHD-ZIP and demonstrated that it is a nuclear-localized, cold-responsive protein that positively contributes to cold stress tolerance. To further investigate the regulatory mechanism underlying CaHD-ZIP function, a yeast two-hybrid (Y2H) screen identified the sucrose non-fermenting 1-related protein kinase CaSNF1 as a previously unrecognized interacting partner of CaHD-ZIP. Their interaction was confirmed by yeast two-hybrid, luciferase complementation imaging, and bimolecular fluorescence complementation assays, with BiFC indicating that the interaction occurs predominantly in the nucleus. In vitro phosphorylation analysis further demonstrated that CaSNF1 directly phosphorylates CaHD-ZIP, providing biochemical evidence for a functional regulatory relationship between these proteins. Complementary loss- and gain-of-function analyses, including virus-induced gene silencing and transient overexpression in pepper together with stable overexpression in Arabidopsis, demonstrated that CaSNF1 positively regulates cold tolerance. Silencing of CaSNF1 increased oxidative damage, impaired antioxidant enzyme activities, and suppressed the expression of antioxidant and cold-responsive genes, whereas overexpression produced the opposite effects and significantly enhanced cold tolerance. Together, these findings identify CaSNF1 as a CaHD-ZIP-interacting kinase and reveal a potential CaSNF1-CaHD-ZIP regulatory module involved in pepper cold stress adaptation. This study advances our understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying pepper cold tolerance and provides potential genetic targets for improving cold resilience in pepper and other Solanaceae crops.

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: Heterologous overexpression of goji LbbHLH36 in tomato Micro Tom was associated with increased total carotenoids, lycopene, and β-carotene in mature fruit. The abstract reports increased expression of early carotenoid biosynthesis genes and increased PSY and PDS enzyme activities, alongside suppressed CCD4 activity.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: The study combines transgene expression, qRT-PCR, enzyme assays, and metabolite analysis, and proposes that enhanced biosynthesis and reduced degradation jointly alter carotenoid accumulation. The abstract does not report evidence of direct binding by LbbHLH36 to the relevant promoters, so it does not establish that the factor directly binds and regulates these target genes.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: The result offers a candidate approach to improving fruit nutritional quality in a Solanaceae crop, but the test organism was tomato and the introduced gene came from goji. Homology, expression patterns, and function in pepper are not validated in the abstract. For pepper ripening TF networks, the idea that both biosynthesis and degradation affect pigment accumulation can be treated as a hypothesis to test, not an established pepper mechanism.

sections.text: Research implication: compare tissue and ripening-stage expression of candidate pigment biosynthesis and degradation genes in the 22-tissue RNA-seq data, and jointly screen for candidate regulatory regions using ATAC-seq and CUT&Tag signals for H3K4me1, H3K4me3, H3K27ac, and H3K27me3; WGBS could add methylation context. These signals can help prioritize candidate relationships with fruit-ripening TF networks and metabolite phenotypes, but co-variation in an atlas is not equivalent to direct regulation.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: The study used heterologous overexpression in tomato Micro Tom, and the abstract does not report evaluation across genetic backgrounds, field performance, or other fruit-quality and yield traits. Expression induction under heat, cold, drought, and salt suggests possible stress–metabolism crosstalk, but the abstract does not demonstrate fruit-pigment improvement under those stress conditions.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: First check whether LbbHLH36 expression, transcription of key biosynthesis genes, PSY/PDS and CCD4 activities, and fruit pigment measurements agree in the transgenic tomatoes. Then examine the tissues and conditions used in the stress-induction experiments, avoiding interpreting expression responses alone as evidence of stress tolerance or fruit-quality benefit.

evidence.abstract: Carotenoids are critical determinants of nutritional quality in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) fruits, and their biosynthesis is tightly regulated by the bHLH transcription factor family. In this study, we investigated the heterologous regulatory function of LbbHLH36, a gene isolated from Lycium barbarum L., in carotenoid accumulation and its responsiveness to abiotic stresses in tomato. The LbbHLH36 coding sequence was cloned into the pNULPGE700 vector and introduced into the model tomato cultivar 'Micro Tom' via Agrobacterium-mediated leaf disc transformation. Quantitative real-time PCR revealed that LbbHLH36 transcript levels peaked in mature fruits of transgenic lines and were associated with significant upregulation of key early biosynthetic genes, including SlPSY1, SlPSY2, SlPDS, and SlZDS. Enzymatic assays further demonstrated increased activities of the rate-limiting enzymes phytoene synthase (PSY) and phytoene desaturase (PDS), alongside a marked suppression of carotenoid cleavage dioxygenase 4 (CCD4) activity in transgenic plants. Metabolomic analyses confirmed that overexpression of LbbHLH36 substantially elevated total carotenoid, lycopene, and β-carotene contents in tomato fruits. Furthermore, LbbHLH36 expression was strongly induced by high temperature, low temperature, drought, and salt stress, suggesting its potential involvement in crosstalk between stress responses and primary metabolism. Collectively, our findings reveal that LbbHLH36 acts as a positive regulator of carotenoid accumulation in tomato through a dual mechanism that concurrently regulate biosynthetic flux and attenuates catabolic degradation, highlighting its value as a candidate gene for nutritional quality improvement in Lycium barbarum, tomato, and other Solanaceous crops.

en.heading: Tomato RIN promotes SlJMJ6 occupancy and cooperatively reduces H3K27me3 at targets, activating ripening-stage carotenoid genes

sections.label: What is new
sections.text: The study proposes that the tomato ripening TF RIN cooperates with the H3K27me3 demethylase SlJMJ6 to promote carotenoid accumulation and activate genes including PSY1, DXS1, and ZISO. SlJMJ6 and RIN co-occupy multiple ripening-associated gene regions, and their association is linked to reduced H3K27me3 at target loci; SlJMJ6 occupancy at representative loci is reduced in the rin mutant.

sections.label: Mechanistic or methodological key point
sections.text: The abstract links RIN-mediated transcriptional regulation with SlJMJ6-mediated chromatin regulation: SlJMJ6 preferentially associates with promoter regions enriched in CArG motifs, and RIN facilitates SlJMJ6 chromatin occupancy. Loss of either factor is accompanied by increased H3K27me3 at target loci and reduced expression of ripening-related genes; the abstract does not specify the chromatin assay platform, so a particular technique such as CUT&Tag cannot be assigned.

sections.label: Relevance to pepper research
sections.text: This study directly connects a fruit-ripening TF network, chromatin modification, and pigment metabolism, offering leads for prioritizing candidate TF–chromatin relationships during pepper ripening. The corresponding RIN-related factors, SlJMJ6 function, and targeting of pigment genes in pepper all remain to be validated; the tomato mechanism should not be treated as an established pepper mechanism.

sections.label: Implications for the 22-tissue atlas
sections.text: Research implication: identify co-expression patterns between ripening-related TFs and pigment biosynthesis genes in the 22-tissue RNA-seq data, then combine them with ATAC-seq and CUT&Tag to examine candidate promoter accessibility and H3K4me1, H3K4me3, H3K27ac, and H3K27me3 distributions; WGBS could add DNA methylation context. Prioritize comparisons across fruit development and ripening stages and candidate ranking in TF networks; if the atlas is not a time series, tissue differences cannot substitute for dynamic evidence during ripening.

sections.label: Limitations
sections.text: The abstract reports genetic and omics analyses and an effect of RIN on SlJMJ6 occupancy, but does not provide the specific assay platforms, a target-locus list, or experimental details. The links among SlJMJ6 occupancy, H3K27me3 changes, and transcriptional responses support the regulatory model, but the abstract alone does not establish a direct molecular causal chain for every target gene, nor does it describe effects of the relevant modifications on other tomato agronomic traits.

sections.label: What to read first
sections.text: First check the evidence for SlJMJ6/RIN co-occupancy, CArG motif enrichment, and reduced SlJMJ6 occupancy in the rin mutant, as well as the correspondence between H3K27me3 changes and target-gene transcription. Then compare the effects of SlJMJ6 or RIN loss on carotenoid phenotypes and ripening-related genes to assess whether the genetic perturbation, chromatin state, and metabolic output evidence is consistent.

evidence.abstract: Fruit ripening involves extensive transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming, yet how chromatin modifiers are targeted to specific genomic loci in coordination with transcription factors remains unclear. Here, we show that the histone H3K27me3 demethylase SlJMJ6 physically and functionally associates with the master ripening regulator RIPENING INHIBITOR (RIN) to regulate carotenoid biosynthesis in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) fruit. Genetic and transcriptional analyses demonstrated that SlJMJ6 and RIN cooperatively promote carotenoid accumulation and activate key biosynthetic genes, including PSY1, DXS1 and ZISO. Genome-wide analyses revealed that SlJMJ6 preferentially binds promoter regions enriched in CArG motifs and extensively co-occupies ripening-associated genes with RIN. Epigenomic analyses showed that SlJMJ6 association correlates with reduced H3K27me3 enrichment at co-targeted loci, whereas loss of either SlJMJ6 or RIN increases H3K27me3 enrichment and reduces expression of ripening-related genes. Furthermore, SlJMJ6 occupancy at representative target loci is markedly reduced in the rin mutant, indicating that RIN facilitates SlJMJ6 chromatin association. Together, our findings reveal a cooperative RIN-SlJMJ6 regulatory module linking RIN-dependent transcriptional regulation with locus-specific H3K27me3 dynamics, providing a mechanistic framework for chromatin-mediated activation of metabolic genes during fruit ripening.
